description: Matches a whole AsciiDoc listing block, its delimiter lines included: its content is listing and is never translated.
regex: (?m:^-{4,}[\x20\t]*$.*?^-{4,}[\x20\t]*$)  # The whole block, delimiter line to delimiter line; (?m) so ^ and $ are line ends, (?s) is global so . crosses lines, lazy so it stops at the first closing delimiter

description: Matches a whole AsciiDoc literal block, its delimiter lines included: its content is literal and is never translated.
regex: (?m:^\.{4,}[\x20\t]*$.*?^\.{4,}[\x20\t]*$)  # The whole block, delimiter line to delimiter line; (?m) so ^ and $ are line ends, (?s) is global so . crosses lines, lazy so it stops at the first closing delimiter

description: Matches a whole AsciiDoc passthrough block, its delimiter lines included: its content is passthrough and is never translated.
regex: (?m:^\+{4,}[\x20\t]*$.*?^\+{4,}[\x20\t]*$)  # The whole block, delimiter line to delimiter line; (?m) so ^ and $ are line ends, (?s) is global so . crosses lines, lazy so it stops at the first closing delimiter

description: Matches a whole AsciiDoc comment block, its delimiter lines included: its content is comment and is never translated.
regex: (?m:^/{4,}[\x20\t]*$.*?^/{4,}[\x20\t]*$)  # The whole block, delimiter line to delimiter line; (?m) so ^ and $ are line ends, (?s) is global so . crosses lines, lazy so it stops at the first closing delimiter

description: Matches an AsciiDoc example (or admonition) block delimiter; the content between two of them is prose.
regex: (?m:^={4,}[\x20\t]*$)  # Four or more equal signs on their own line

description: Matches an AsciiDoc sidebar block delimiter; the content between two of them is prose.
regex: (?m:^\*{4,}[\x20\t]*$)  # Four or more asterisks on their own line

description: Matches an AsciiDoc table delimiter; the cells between two of them are prose.
Matches the marker of an AsciiDoc section title (= Title through ===== Title); the title text is translatable.
regex: (?m:^={1,5}[\x20\t]+)  # One to five equal signs at the start of a line, then spaces; the title follows

description: Matches an AsciiDoc document attribute entry (:attribute-name: value), kept as it is.
Matches an AsciiDoc block attribute line ([source,yaml], [cols=...], [NOTE], [.role]), kept as it is.
regex: (?m:^\[[^\]\n]*\][\x20\t]*$)  # [source,yaml], [cols="1,2"], [NOTE], [%header], [.role] on their own line

description: Matches an AsciiDoc comment line, kept as it is.
regex: (?m:^//[^\n]*$)  # A line starting with //; a URL's // is never at a line start

description: Matches AsciiDoc conditional directives (ifdef, ifndef, ifeval, endif).
regex: (?m:^(ifdef|ifndef|ifeval|endif)::[^\[\n]*\[[^\]\n]*\])  # ifdef::attr[] and the like

description: Matches AsciiDoc include directives.
regex: (?m:^include::[^\[\n]+\[[^\]\n]*\])  # include::file[attrs]

description: Matches the AsciiDoc block image macro; its alternative text is kept as it is.
regex: (?m:^image::[^\[\n]+\[[^\]\n]*\])  # image::file[attrs] on its own line

description: Matches an AsciiDoc thematic break.
regex: (?m:^'{3}[\x20\t]*$)  # Three single quotes on their own line

description: Matches an AsciiDoc page break.
regex: (?m:^<{3,}[\x20\t]*$)  # Three or more less-than signs on their own line

description: Matches an AsciiDoc list item marker (bulleted, numbered, or hyphen); the item text is translatable.
Matches the marker of an AsciiDoc block title (.Title); the title text is translatable.
regex: (?m:^\.(?=[A-Za-z]))  # A dot at the start of a line, before a letter

description: Matches an AsciiDoc table cell separator; each cell is translatable.
regex: (?m:^[\x20\t]*\|[\x20\t]*)|[\x20\t]+\|[\x20\t]+  # A cell separator: a bar at the start of a line, or between spaces

description: Matches an AsciiDoc anchor ([[anchor-id]]).
Matches an AsciiDoc attribute reference ({attribute-name}).
regex: \{[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\}  # {attribute-name}

description: Matches an AsciiDoc cross-reference to an anchor (<<anchor>> or <<anchor,display text>>).
Matches AsciiDoc monospace text (`code`), kept as it is: a command or a name is not translated.
regex: `[^`\n]+`  # Text in backticks: code, a command, a file name

description: Matches AsciiDoc inline passthrough text (+text+), kept as it is.
Matches AsciiDoc footnote macros.
regex: footnote(ref)?:\[[^\]\n]*\]  # footnote:[text]

description: Matches AsciiDoc inline macros whose content is not prose (kbd:[Ctrl+C], image:file[], mailto:…).
regex: (mailto|btn|kbd|menu|pass|stem|latexmath|asciimath|image|icon):[^\[\s]*\[[^\]\n]*\]  # macro:target[content], kept whole

description: Matches an AsciiDoc callout marker.
Matches AsciiDoc superscript.
Matches AsciiDoc subscript.
Matches the closing bracket of an AsciiDoc xref or link label.
regex: \]  # The closing bracket of a link label

description: Matches the opening of an AsciiDoc xref or link macro up to its bracket: the target is kept, the label that follows is translatable.
regex: (xref|link):[^\[\s]+\[  # xref:page.adoc[ or link:https://…[ ; the label follows

description: Matches the AsciiDoc bold closing marker.
Matches the AsciiDoc bold opening marker.
regex: (?<![\w\*])\*(?=[^\s\*])  # Bold opening marker: not after a word or another *, before a character

description: Matches the AsciiDoc italic closing marker.
regex: (?<=\S)_(?=\s|[.,;:!?\)\]]|$)  # Italic closing marker

description: Matches the AsciiDoc italic opening marker.
regex: (?<![\w_])_(?=[^\s_])  # Italic opening marker: not after a word or another _, before a character

description: Matches the AsciiDoc highlight closing marker.
regex: (?<=\S)\#(?=\s|[.,;:!?\)\]]|$)  # Highlight closing marker

description: Matches the AsciiDoc highlight opening marker.
regex: (?<![\w\#])\#(?=[^\s\#])  # Highlight opening marker

description: Matches a sentence-final mark at the end of a line that a structural line follows (a blank line, a block delimiter or attribute line, a list item, a table row, a heading, a directive): the mark alone is the break, so the newline stays for the structural rule.
regex: (?m:[.!?:](?=[\x20\t]*\n[\x20\t]*(?:\n|[\[|*.=\-:/<]|image::|include::|ifn?def::|endif::|$)))  # the mark, looking ahead at the structural line

description: Matches a Japanese full stop or dot followed by whitespace.
regex:
[。．]   # Match a Japanese full stop (。) or dot (．)
\s+     # Followed by one or more whitespace characters

description: Matches one or more Japanese characters (Hiragana, Katakana, Kanji).
regex: [\p{IsHiragana}\p{IsKatakana}\p{IsHan}]+  # Match one or more Japanese characters

description: Matches CJK symbols and punctuation followed by whitespace.
regex: \p{InCJK_Symbols_and_Punctuation}+\s+  # One or more CJK symbols and punctuation characters

description: Matches common acronyms and abbreviations.
regex: L\.P\. | Alt\. | Approx\. | E\.G\. | O\. | Maj\. | Misc\. | P\.O\. | J\.D\. | Jam\. | Card\. | Dec\. | Sept\. | MR\. | Long\. | Hat\. | G\. | Link\. | DC\. | D\.C\. | M\.T\. | Hz\. | Mrs\. | By\. | Act\. | Var\. | N\.V\. | Aug\. | B\. | S\.A\. | Up\. | Job\. | Num\. | M\.I\.T\. | Ok\. | Org\. | Ex\. | Cont\. | U\. | Mart\. | Fn\. | Abs\. | Lt\. | OK\. | Z\. | E\. | Kb\. | Est\. | A\.M\. | L\.A\. | Prof\. | U\.S\. | Nov\. | Ph\.D\. | Mar\. | I\.T\. | exec\. | Jan\. | N\.Y\. | X\. | Md\. | Op\. | vs\. | D\.A\. | A\.D\. | R\.L\. | P\.M\. | Or\. | M\.R\. | Cap\. | PC\. | Feb\. | Exec\. | I\.e\. | Sep\. | Gb\. | K\. | U\.S\.C\. | Mt\. | S\. | A\.S\. | C\.O\.D\. | Capt\. | Col\. | In\. | C\.F\. | Adj\. | AD\. | I\.D\. | Mgr\. | R\.T\. | B\.V\. | M\. | Conn\. | Yr\. | Rev\. | Phys\. | pp\. | Ms\. | To\. | Sgt\. | J\.K\. | Nr\. | Jun\. | Fri\. | S\.A\.R\. | Lev\. | Lt\.Cdr\. | Def\. | F\. | Do\. | Joe\. | Id\. | Mr\. | Dept\. | Is\. | Pvt\. | Diff\. | Hon\.B\.A\. | Q\. | Mb\. | On\. | Min\. | J\.B\. | Ed\. | AB\. | A\. | S\.p\.A\. | I\. | a\.m\. | Comm\. | Go\. | VS\. | L\. | All\. | PP\. | P\.V\. | T\. | K\.R\. | Etc\. | D\. | Adv\. | Lib\. | E\.g\. | Pro\. | U\.S\.A\. | S\.E\. | AA\. | Rep\. | Sq\. | As\. | St\. | Dr\. | Dra\. | Jr\. | Messrs\. | Sr\. | Sra\. | Srta\. | Dña\. | Ud\. | Uds\. | Vd\. | Vds\.

description: Matches email addresses.
regex:
<?                      # Optional opening angle bracket
[a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+       # Local part: one or more allowed characters
@                       # At symbol
[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+          # Domain: one or more allowed characters
\.                      # Dot before TLD
[a-zA-Z]{2,}            # TLD: at least two alphabetic characters
>?                      # Optional closing angle bracket

description: Matches a single quote character.
regex: '  # Single quote character

description: Matches double quote or Unicode quotation marks.
regex: [\"\p{Pf}\p{Pi}]  # Match double quote, final punctuation, or initial punctuation

description: Matches two or more newlines: in AsciiDoc the end of a paragraph, kept in the template.
regex: \n{2,}  # Match two or more newline characters

description: Matches integer and floating-point numbers.
regex:
\d+                # One or more digits
(\.\d+)?           # Optional decimal point followed by one or more digits
(?=                # Lookahead to ensure the number is followed by:
    [\s\)\]\}\[\"\.=<]  # Whitespace, closing parenthesis, closing bracket, closing brace, opening bracket, double quote, period, or equal sign
    | $            # Or the end of the string
)

description: Matches compound capitalized words (e.g., Hello-world).
regex:
[\p{Lu}]                # Match an uppercase letter
[\p{Ll}]+               # Followed by one or more lowercase letters
-                       # Followed by a hyphen
(                       # Start of group:
    [\p{Ll}'-]+         # Match one or more lowercase letters, apostrophes, or hyphens
    |                   # OR
    [\p{Lu}][\p{Ll}]    # Match an uppercase letter followed by a lowercase letter
)                       # End of group
(?=                     # Lookahead to ensure the match is followed by:
    [\s</&\(\)\[\]\{\}\p{Pf}\p{Pi}"-]  # Whitespace, punctuation, or special characters
    |                   # OR
    [\.。．,:;"?!][\s<&>]  # Punctuation followed by whitespace or special characters
    |                   # OR
    [\.。．:?\)]$         # Punctuation at the end of the string
    |                   # OR
    $                   # End of string
)

description: Matches compound lowercase words (e.g., word-compound).
regex:
[\p{Ll}]+                # One or more lowercase letters
-                        # Hyphen
(                        # Start of group for the second part of the compound word
    [\p{Ll}'-]+          # One or more lowercase letters, apostrophes, or hyphens
    |                    # OR
    [\p{Lu}][\p{Ll}'-]+  # An uppercase letter followed by one or more lowercase letters, apostrophes, or hyphens
)                        # End of group
(?=                      # Lookahead to ensure the compound word is followed by specific characters
    [\s</&\(\)\[\]\{\}\p{Pf}\p{Pi}"-]  # Whitespace, punctuation, or certain HTML entities
    |                    # OR
    [\.。．,:;"?!][\s<&>]  # Punctuation followed by whitespace or certain HTML entities
    |                    # OR
    [\.。．:?\)]$          # Punctuation at the end of the string
    | $                  # End of string
)

description: Matches compound uppercase words (e.g., HELLO-WORLD).
regex:
([\p{Lu}]+                # First part: one or more uppercase letters
|[\p{Lu}\'-]+)            # or uppercase letters with optional apostrophes or hyphens
-                         # Hyphen separating the two parts
([\p{Lu}\'-]+             # Second part: one or more uppercase letters with optional apostrophes or hyphens
|[\p{Ll}\'-]+             # or one or more lowercase letters with optional apostrophes or hyphens
|[\p{Lu}][\p{Ll}\'-]+)    # or one uppercase letter followed by one or more lowercase letters with optional apostrophes or hyphens
(?=                       # Lookahead to ensure the match is followed by specific characters
    [\s</&\(\)\[\]\{\}\p{Pf}\p{Pi}\"-]  # Whitespace, punctuation, or specific characters
    |[\.。．,:;\"\?!][\s<&>]            # or punctuation followed by whitespace or specific characters
    |[\.。．:?\)]$                      # or punctuation at the end of the string
    |$                                 # or end of the string
)

description: Matches a capitalized word (e.g., Alex's).
regex:
[\p{Lu}]            # Match an uppercase letter
[\p{Ll}]+           # Followed by one or more lowercase letters
(                   # Start of optional group
    [\'\u2019]           # Match an apostrophe or right single quotation mark
    \p{Ll}+         # Followed by one or more lowercase letters
)*                  # Zero or more occurrences of the optional group
(?=                 # Positive lookahead for word boundaries or punctuation
    [\?!]{2,}[\s<&>\"\p{Pf}']  # A run of question or exclamation marks, then a space, a quote or markup
    |                   # OR
    [\?!]{2,}$          # A run of them at the end of the string
    |                   # OR
    [\s</&\(\)\[\]\{\}\p{Pf}\p{Pi}\"-]  # Match whitespace, HTML tags, punctuation, or special characters
    |               # OR
    [\.。．,:;\"“\?!][\s<&>]  # Match punctuation followed by whitespace or special characters
    |               # OR
    [\.。．:?\)]$    # Match punctuation at the end of the string
    | $             # OR end of string
)

description: Matches a lowercase word, potentially with apostrophes (e.g., it's).
regex:
[\p{Ll}]+                # One or more lowercase letters
(                        # Start of group for apostrophe and following letters
    [\'\u2019]                # Apostrophe or right single quotation mark
    \p{Ll}+              # One or more lowercase letters
)*                       # Zero or more occurrences of the group
(?=                      # Positive lookahead to ensure the match is followed by specific characters
    [\?!]{2,}[\s<&>\"\p{Pf}']  # A run of question or exclamation marks, then a space, a quote or markup
    |                   # OR
    [\?!]{2,}$          # A run of them at the end of the string
    |                   # OR
    [\s</&\(\)\[\]\{\}\p{Pf}\p{Pi}\"\'-*_`#]  # Whitespace, punctuation, or specific symbols (incl. AsciiDoc markers)
    |                    # OR
    [\.。．,:;\"\'\?!][\"\'“\s<&>]  # Punctuation followed by specific symbols or whitespace
    |                    # OR
    [\.。．:?\)]$         # Punctuation at the end of the string
    | $                  # End of the string
)

description: Matches a sequence of uppercase letters, optionally with apostrophes.
regex:
[\p{Lu}]+                # One or more uppercase letters
(                        # Optional group for apostrophe and lowercase letters
    [\'\u2019]                # Apostrophe or right single quotation mark
    \p{Ll}+              # One or more lowercase letters
)*                       # Zero or more occurrences of the optional group
(?=                      # Lookahead assertion
    [\?!]{2,}[\s<&>\"\p{Pf}']  # A run of question or exclamation marks, then a space, a quote or markup
    |                   # OR
    [\?!]{2,}$          # A run of them at the end of the string
    |                   # OR
    [\s</&\(\)\[\]\{\}\p{Pf}\p{Pi}\"\'-*_`#]  # Whitespace, punctuation, or special characters (incl. AsciiDoc markers)
    |                    # OR
    [\.。．,:;\"\'“\?!][\"\'“\s<&>]  # Punctuation followed by certain characters
    |                    # OR
    [\.。．:?\)]$         # Punctuation at the end of the string
    | $                  # End of string
)

description: Matches camelCase or mixed-case words.
regex:
[\p{Lu}\p{Ll}]+                # One or more Unicode uppercase or lowercase letters
(?=                            # Positive lookahead for boundary characters
    [\?!]{2,}[\s<&>\"\p{Pf}']  # A run of question or exclamation marks, then a space, a quote or markup
    |                   # OR
    [\?!]{2,}$          # A run of them at the end of the string
    |                   # OR
    [\s</&\(\)\[\]\{\}\p{Pf}\p{Pi}\"\'-*_`#]  # Whitespace, punctuation, and symbols (incl. AsciiDoc markers)
    |                          # OR
    [\.。．,:;\"“\?!][\"\'“\s<&>]  # Punctuation followed by specific characters
    |                          # OR
    [\.。．:?\)]$               # Punctuation at the end of the string
    | $                        # End of string
)

description: Matches an ellipsis (two or more periods).
regex:
\.{2,}          # Match two or more consecutive periods
\s?             # Optionally match a single whitespace character
(?=[<&>]|$)     # Lookahead to ensure the next character is '<', '&', '>', or the end of the string

description: Matches a period followed by whitespace before specific characters.
regex:
\.              # Match a literal period
\s+             # Match one or more whitespace characters
(?=             # Positive lookahead to ensure the following condition is met
    [<&>\"\p{Lu}\p{Pi}¿¡—]|$    # one of <, &, >, ", an uppercase letter, an opening quote, ¿, ¡ or a dialogue dash (—), or end of string
)

description: Matches a period at the end of the string.
regex:
\.      # Match a literal dot (.)
(?=$)   # Assert that what follows is the end of the string

description: Matches a comma followed by whitespace or special characters.
regex:
,                # Match a literal comma
(?=              # Positive lookahead to assert what follows the comma
    [\s<&>]      # Match any whitespace character or HTML special characters (&, <, >)
    |            # OR
    $            # End of the string
)

description: Matches an equal sign.
regex: =   # Matches the equal sign character

description: Matches a colon followed by optional whitespace.
regex:
:                # Match a literal colon
\s*              # Match zero or more whitespace characters
(?=              # Positive lookahead to ensure what follows is:
    [<&>\p{Lu}\p{Ll}]|$   # <, >, &, upper/lower Unicode letter, or end of string
)

description: Matches a single forward slash.
regex: /  # Match a single forward slash

description: Matches a semicolon followed by whitespace or special characters.
regex:
;                # Match a semicolon
(?=              # Positive lookahead to assert what follows the semicolon
    [\s<&>]      # Match any whitespace character, or one of the characters: <, &, >
    |            # OR
    $            # End of the string
)

description: Matches optional whitespace followed by an open parenthesis.
regex:
\s*    # Zero or more whitespace characters
\(     # Open parenthesis

description: Matches a closing parenthesis followed by optional whitespace.
regex:
\)      # Closing parenthesis
\s*     # Zero or more whitespace characters

description: Matches optional whitespace followed by an open square bracket.
regex:
\s*    # Match zero or more whitespace characters
\[     # Match an open square bracket '['

description: Matches a closing square bracket followed by optional whitespace.
regex:
\]       # Match a closing square bracket
\s*      # Match zero or more whitespace characters

description: Matches optional whitespace followed by an opening curly bracket.
regex:
\s*    # Match zero or more whitespace characters
\{     # Match an opening curly bracket '{'

description: Matches a closing curly bracket followed by optional whitespace.
regex:
\}       # Closing curly bracket
\s*      # Zero or more whitespace characters

description: Matches a dash surrounded by whitespace.
regex:
\s    # Leading whitespace character
-     # Dash character
\s    # Trailing whitespace character

description: Matches an em dash character.
regex: \u2014  # Unicode code point for em dash (—)

description: Matches a table cell separator between spaces or after a newline, kept in the template.
regex:
\s      # Match any whitespace character
\|      # Match the vertical bar character '|'
\s      # Match any whitespace character

description: Matches a single dash character.
regex: -  # Match a single dash character

description: Matches a single vertical bar character.
regex: \|  # Matches a single vertical bar character

description: This regular expression matches a run of question or exclamation marks, with any closing quotes after it, where a new sentence or the end of the text follows. A lower-case word after it continues the sentence, as Spanish writes a speech verb after a question or exclamation (RAE: '¡Ya voy! dijo él') and English a speech tag after a closing quote ('"Sir?" says the doctor').
regex:
[?!]+[\"\p{Pf}']*  # A run of question or exclamation marks, with the closing quotes right after it,
(?=                 # ending a sentence only where another starts or the text ends:
    \s*$            # the end of the string
    |
    \s+[\p{Lu}\p{N}¿¡—\"\p{Pi}'<&]  # a space, then a capital, a digit, ¿, ¡, a dash, an opening quote or markup
    |
    [<&]            # markup right after
    |
    [\p{IsHiragana}\p{IsKatakana}\p{IsHan}]  # Japanese or Chinese text
)

description: Matches inverted question mark or exclamation mark.
regex: [¿¡]  # Match either the inverted question mark (¿) or the inverted exclamation mark (¡)

description: Matches two or more consecutive whitespace characters.
regex: \s{2,}  # Match two or more consecutive whitespace characters

description: Matches any single whitespace character.
regex: \s  # Matches any whitespace character (space, tab, newline, etc.)

description: Matches URLs with common schemes.
regex:
(ftp|file|http|https)://  # URL scheme: ftp, file, http, or https followed by '://'
[^\s\(\)\]\[\"\'<]+       # One or more characters that are not whitespace or specific punctuation
[^\.\"\'<]                # A character that is not a period, double quote, single quote, or less-than sign
(?=[\s\(\)\]\[\"\.\'<]|$) # Lookahead to ensure the URL is followed by whitespace, specific punctuation, or end of string

description: Matches symbol-like sequences that don't fit other categories.
regex:
[^\s\(\)\[\]\{\}\"\'=<*_`#\p{IsHiragana}\p{IsKatakana}\p{IsHan}]+  # Start: Exclude specific characters (incl. AsciiDoc markers *_`#)
[^:\.\"\'\)\(\{\}\[\]=<*_`#]                                      # End: Exclude specific characters (incl. AsciiDoc markers *_`#)
(?=[\s\(\)\[\]\"\'\.=<*_`#]|$|\s+$)                               # Followed by: Specific characters or end of string

description: Matches any single character not matched by previous rules.
regex: .    # Match any character except a newline
